label: John Greenewald Jr.
narrative: Greenewald is the private citizen who has done more than any institution to build the documentary base this board runs on. He began filing FOIA requests as a teenager in 1996 and has since obtained and published well over two million pages. Two of his releases are load-bearing for the 1970s-2000s era: DoD FOIA case 97-F-1677, processed by the Office of the Assistant Secretary of Defense in September 1997, which produced the Halt memorandum on Rendlesham and the November 1975 Malmstrom AFB overflight records; and his 2013 Mandatory Declassification Review of the entire NSA UFO holding, which forced further release of documents NSA had previously produced with only a few words visible per page. In 2025 he became the principal test of the Pentagon's own honesty about disinformation: after the Wall Street Journal reported that the Secretary of Defense's office had issued a spring 2023 memo ordering an end to an Air Force practice of falsely telling personnel they were on a reverse-engineering programme, Greenewald filed for the memo. OSD responded in September 2025 that no such record existed; AFOSI said it had no records of any such investigation; the Pentagon spokesperson said in October 2025 she could not confirm the memo existed. In December 2025 an OSD appellate authority granted his appeal and remanded for a new search. That sequence - press claim, government no-records finding, appeal, remand - is the mechanism by which this board's evidence is actually produced.
